long_biography.plain_text:
Frank Meyer's backing turned Ken Griffin's successful Harvard trading into the institutional fund that became Citadel. Griffin had traded convertible bonds using market data from a satellite dish on his dormitory roof. He developed the new firm around quantitative analysis, powerful software and specialist teams, establishing the investment-management business at the centre of his career.

Griffin and his partners later created Citadel Securities as options markets moved towards electronic trading, building a separate market-making company. Griffin Catalyst now organises his civic work across education, medical research and community opportunity. One gift helped open the Kenneth C. Griffin Cancer Research Building in Miami, doubling the university's dedicated cancer-research space.
